# Overview
 
In this document, we perform a descriptive analysis to investigate whether autotomy in *Jussara sp.* differs between leg types (I, II, III, or IV), side of the body (right or left) and populations (2002, 2009, 2011, 2012), and whether this information should be preserved in the permutation analyses.

We also perform two additional premise tests: we test whether legs of different types (I, II, III or IV) differ in overall length, and whether amputation probability differs between sex and leg identity.

```{r calling Rpackages, echo=FALSE}
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
library(lme4)
library(DHARMa)
library(emmeans)
library(glmmTMB)
```

# Load data

The data frame `main_data` contains information on autotomy in *Jussara* sp. according to individual `id` (ranging from 1 to 1405), `population` (2002, 2009, 2011, and 2012), leg identity (`leg_id`: r1 to r4, l1 to l4), and autotomy status of each leg (`autotomy`: 0 or 1). The data frame also includes the columns `leg` and `side`, which correspond to information separated from `leg_id`.

```{r echo=FALSE}
main_data <- readRDS(file = here("data","processed","main_data.rds"))

head(main_data)
```

The data frame `sex_data` contains information on individual `id` (not necessarily corresponding to those in `main_data` and `leg_length_data`), sex, leg identity and the  autotomy status of each leg pair (ranging from 0 to 2 autotomies).

```{r echo=FALSE}
sex_data <- readRDS(file = here("data","processed","sex_data.rds"))

head(sex_data)
```

The data frame `leg_length_data` contains information on individual id (not necessarily corresponding to those in `main_data` and `sex_data`), leg identity, and leg length for 10 individuals collected in 2002.

```{r echo=FALSE}
leg_length_data <- readRDS(file = here("data","processed","leg_length_data.rds"))

head(leg_length_data)
```

# Exploratory analysis

```{r echo=FALSE}
df_n <- data.frame(
  population = c("2002", "2009", "2011", "2012", 'Total'),
  n = c("n = 380", "n = 485", "n = 208", "n = 332", "n = 1405"),
  na = c("n = 159", "n = 221", "n = 102", "n = 123", "n = 605"),
  a = c("n = 206", "n = 342", "n = 132", "n = 157", "n = 837")
)

# number of autotomized legs per individual
df_autotomy <- main_data %>%
  group_by(population, id) %>%
  summarise(
    total = sum(autotomy),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(population, total) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ind = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(population) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_ind_pop = n_ind / sum(n_ind)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# total across all populations
df_autotomy_total <- main_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    total = sum(autotomy),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(total) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ind = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_ind_pop = n_ind / sum(n_ind),
    population = "Total"
  )

# combining
df_autotomy <- bind_rows(df_autotomy, df_autotomy_total)

# factor ordering
df_autotomy <- df_autotomy %>%
  mutate(
    population = factor(
      population,
      levels = c("2002", "2009", "2011", "2012", "Total")
    ),
    total = factor(
      total,
      levels = 0:4
    )
  )
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
# Fig 2A
Fig_2A <- ggplot(
  df_autotomy,
  aes(x = population,
      y = perc_ind_pop,
      fill = total)
) +

  geom_bar(
    stat = "identity",
    color = "black",
    width = 0.7
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = df_n,
    aes(x = population, y = 1.02, label = n),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4,
    vjust = 0
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(c("0" = "white", 
                 "1"="gray10", 
                 "2"="gray40", 
                 "3"="gray70", 
                 "4"="gray90")),
    labels = c(
      "0" = "Non-autotomized",
      "1" = "1 leg lost",
      "2" = "2 legs lost",
      "3" = "3 legs lost",
      "4" = "4 legs lost"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1.08),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Individuals (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +

  annotate(
    "text",
    x = Inf,
    y = Inf,
    label = "A",
    hjust = 1.1,
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 6,
    fontface = "bold"
  )
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
# percentage of autotomies by body side within each population
df_side <- main_data %>%
  group_by(population, side) %>%
  summarise(
    autotomy = sum(autotomy),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(population) %>%
  mutate(
    total_aut = sum(autotomy),
    perc_aut_side = autotomy / total_aut
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# total across all populations
df_total_side <- main_data %>%
  group_by(side) %>%
  summarise(
    autotomy = sum(autotomy),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_aut = sum(autotomy),
    perc_aut_side = autotomy / total_aut,
    population = "Total"
  )

# combining datasets
df_side <- bind_rows(df_side, df_total_side)

# ordering factors
df_side <- df_side %>%
  mutate(
    population = factor(
      population,
      levels = c("2002", "2009", "2011", "2012", "Total")
    ),
    side = factor(
      side,
      levels = c("left", "right")
    )
  )
```

df_sex <- sex_data %>%

# Premise tests

## 1) Are there size differences between the different types of legs?

Harvestmen legs typically differ both structurally and functionally. To evaluate whether *Jussara* sp. legs are structurally distinct, we test whether leg types differ in absolute size. Field observations suggest that Leg II is visibly the longest, but it is unclear whether Legs I, III, and IV also differ.

We fit a mixed model assuming that each individual has its own baseline size, while the effect of leg type is consistent across individuals.

The ANOVA indicates a strong effect of leg type on size. Pairwise comparisons suggest the pattern:

**Leg II > Leg IV > Leg I $\approx$ Leg III**

```{r echo=FALSE}
boxplot_leglength <- ggplot(leg_length_data, aes(x = leg_id, y = length)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("I", "II", "III", "IV")) +
  labs(
    x = "Leg identity",
    y = "Leg length (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
  )
```

### Descriptive mean and sd

```{r}
# mean
aggregate(leg_length_data$length, by = list(leg_length_data$leg_id), mean)

# sd
aggregate(leg_length_data$length, by = list(leg_length_data$leg_id), sd)
```

```{r}
# since there is repetition, we should use Individual as a random factor
mleg <- lmer(length ~ leg_id + (1 | id), data = leg_length_data)
```

```{r}
simulateResiduals(mleg, plot = T)

summary(mleg)

anova(mleg)

emmeans(mleg, pairwise ~ leg_id)
```

## 2) Are autotomy probabilities different between sexes?

To evaluate whether autotomy probability differs between males and females, we fitted a series of binomial GLMMs including leg identity and sex as explanatory variables. Individual identity was initially included as a random intercept.

We first fitted the full model including the interaction between sex and leg identity.

```{r}
# cbind(sucesses,failures)
msexfull <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(autotomy, 2 - autotomy) ~ sex*leg_id + (1|id),
  family = binomial,
  data = sex_data
)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
simulateResiduals(msexfull, plot = T)

summary(msexfull)
```

We then removed the interaction term.

```{r}
msexadd <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(autotomy, 2 - autotomy) ~ sex + leg_id + (1|id),
  family = binomial,
  data = sex_data
)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
simulateResiduals(msexadd, plot = T)

summary(msexadd)
```

Finally, we fitted a model containing only leg identity.

```{r}
msexbase <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(autotomy, 2 - autotomy) ~ leg_id + (1|id),
  family = binomial,
  data = sex_data
)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
simulateResiduals(msexbase, plot = T)

summary(msexbase)
```

Models were compared using likelihood ratio tests and AIC values.

```{r}
anova(msexfull,msexadd,msexbase)
```

Removing the interaction between sex and leg identity did not reduce model fit, nor did removing the main effect of sex. The simplest model, containing only leg identity, presented the lowest AIC. Additionally, the variance associated with the random intercept of individual identity was effectively zero, indicating little residual heterogeneity among individuals after accounting for leg type.

Together, these results provide no evidence that males and females differ in autotomy probability in *Jussara* sp. Instead, autotomy probability appears to be primarily explained by leg identity.

## 3) Does autotomy probability vary across leg identity, body side, and population?

We fitted a series of generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) to evaluate whether the probability of autotomy varies across leg identity, body side, and population, while accounting for repeated measurements within individuals. All models included a random intercept for individual identity (id), which captures among-individual heterogeneity and the non-independence of the eight legs measured per individual.

We started from an additive model including leg type, body side, and year as fixed effects. To assess the contribution of each predictor, this model was compared against reduced models excluding one fixed effect at a time.

## Additive model

We fitted a model including side, leg, and population as fixed effects, and a random intercept for individual identity. Population was treated as a fixed effect due to the small number of levels (four), allowing direct estimation of differences in autotomy probability among sampling years.

Grouped residual diagnostics did not reveal significant dispersion when structured by leg, population, side, or individual identity, indicating that the additive model adequately captures the main sources of variation in autotomy probability.

```{r}
mlegsidepopadd <- glmmTMB(autotomy ~ side + leg + population + (1|id), 
                          family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
                          data = main_data)

mlegsidepopadd_sim <- simulateResiduals(mlegsidepopadd, plot = T)

# group by individual
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mlegsidepopadd_sim, group = main_data$id))

# group by leg
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mlegsidepopadd_sim, group = main_data$leg))

# group by side
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mlegsidepopadd_sim, group = main_data$side))

# group by population
testDispersion(recalculateResiduals(mlegsidepopadd_sim, group = main_data$population))
```

## One-factor-at-a-time comparisons

To evaluate the contribution of each predictor to baseline variation in autotomy probability, we performed one-factor-at-a-time model comparisons using likelihood ratio tests implemented via the `drop1` function. This procedure sequentially removes each fixed effect from the full additive model while retaining all other predictors and the random intercept for `id`.

These results indicate that permutation procedures should preserve variation associated with leg identity and population, whereas body side does not represent a strong source of structured heterogeneity in baseline autotomy probability and may not require explicit conditioning in the null model.

```{r}
drop1(mlegsidepopadd, test = "Chisq")
```

## Final model

Given the lack of evidence for an effect of body side, it was excluded from the final model used for estimation.

```{r final model}
mlegpop <- glmmTMB(autotomy ~ leg + population + (1|id),
                   family = binomial,
                   data = main_data)

simulateResiduals(mlegpop, plot = T)

summary(mlegpop)
```

# Marginal probabilities

Estimated probabilities revealed a consistent pattern across populations, with leg II showing the highest probability of autotomy and leg III the lowest, while legs I and IV showed intermediate values. Although overall probabilities varied among populations, the relative ranking of leg types was conserved, indicating a stable functional structure in susceptibility to autotomy.

```{r marginal (population-level) probabilities}
emm <- emmeans(mlegpop, ~ leg + population, type = "response")
emm <- as.data.frame(emm)

emmeans(mlegpop, ~ leg, type = "response")
pairs(emmeans(mlegpop, ~ leg, type = "response"))

emmeans(mlegpop, ~ population, type = "response")
pairs(emmeans(mlegpop, ~ population, type = "response"))
```

```{r Graphic [PROBABILITIY OF AUTOTOMY], echo=FALSE}
Fig_3 = ggplot(emm, 
                aes(
                  x = factor(leg), 
                  y = prob, 
                  # shape = population,

                  )

    "#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#E15759", "#76B7B2"))+
  # scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 15, 8, 17))+
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 0.2),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.2, by = 0.05),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    #shape = "Year",

  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(r = 40)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 20)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 20)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),

    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```
